01.r: Gives the reason for what the previous verse said: the Levites have no land because the tithe is theirs instead.
01.n: The DRC follows a Latin text that words this verse quite differently, so most of its words do not line up with the Hebrew.

02.r: Marks 'the tithe' as the object of 'I have given'.
02.n: This small word marks a definite direct object and has no English equivalent; it is counted here with 'the tithe of'.

03.r: The tenth part of Israel's produce.
03.n: Gesenius: tithes, from the noun for 'ten'. Our register renders this word 'tithe'.

04.n: STEPBible tags this occurrence with the sense 'descendant, people'. The BSB says 'the Israelites'.

06.r: Introduces what Israel does with the tithe.

07.r: Israel sets the tithe aside for the LORD.
07.n: The causative form of a verb meaning 'be high, rise': literally 'they cause to rise', 'they lift up'. The noun 'contribution' that follows comes from the same root.

08.r: The tithe is given to the LORD before it goes to the Levites.

09.r: The tithe counts as a portion set apart for God.
09.n: From the same root as 'lift up'. Gesenius: an oblation, offering, gift, especially a gift brought to the temple and the priests. Our register renders it 'contribution', not the KJV's 'heave offering'.

10.r: The LORD hands on to the Levites what Israel gave him.
10.n: A perfect: the grant is made and settled.

12.r: The tithe takes the place of the land the Levites do not receive.
12.n: Gesenius notes the noun is often used of the territory assigned to each tribe. That the tithe stands where land would stand is a reasonable reading here, given the verse's closing words.

13.n: Literally 'on so', that is, 'on this ground'; counted with 'Therefore'.

14.r: Draws the conclusion from the grant of the tithe.

15.r: The LORD refers to his ruling about the Levites.

16.n: The preposition can mean 'to' or 'concerning'; the YLT reads 'of them'.

17.r: Within the tribes when the land is shared out.

s: they shall take as an inheritance
21.r: The Levites take no tribal land.
21.n: Gesenius: to receive any thing as a possession. The Geneva has 'ye', as if the words were spoken to the Levites.

22.r: A tribal share of the land.
22.n: Verb and noun share a root: literally 'they shall not inherit an inheritance'.

07.n: ἀφορίζω, mark off, set apart, where the Hebrew has 'lift up'.

09.n: ἀφαίρεμα, a thing taken off, a portion removed and set aside.

11.n: The brief marks the dictionary form as loose.

12.n: ἐν κλήρῳ, 'as a lot': κλῆρος is a lot, and so a share assigned by lot. English 'clergy' comes from this word, by way of Latin.

14.n: διὰ τοῦτο, 'because of this'. The brief marks the dictionary form as loose; τοῦτο is the neuter of οὗτος.

22.n: κλῆρον, 'a lot', where earlier in the verse the Greek also uses this word for the Levites' 'inheritance'.
